call_points.text: Management expects room air conditioning industry to double by 2030 with a CAGR of 18% to 20%.
Prices have been increased by about 8% to cover raw material and BEE norm changes, with more increases expected.
EMP order bookings grew 35% in Q4 driven by Buildings, Data Centers, and Factories.
Commercial AC order inflow gained momentum from government, industrial, and retail segments.
Room AC saw reasonable growth as primary demand picked up in March for summer stocking.
Deep freezers and cold rooms remained stagnant, but storage water coolers saw double-digit growth.
US expansion is progressing well and supplies to Europe have commenced despite tariff uncertainties.
Industrial solutions grew on automotive and steel demand, while Med-Tech slowed on regulatory ambiguity.
Recognised an exceptional one-time impact of ₹38 Cr towards Gratuity and Leave Encashment under New Labour Codes.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The disputes with the Service Tax Authority, West Bengal was with respect to short payment of service tax and incorrect CENVAT credit availed. The Company had disclosed the contingent liability of Rs 91.24 crores under the said matter. Aggrieved by the order passed by the Commissioner against the Company, appeal was filed by the Company along with a pre-deposit of Rs.4.95 crores for the said case. The matter was heard by CESTAT on February 7, 2024. Upon hearing both the parties, the CESTAT passed an order remanding the matter back to the Adjudicating Authority to, inter alia, examine the documents filed by the Company and to pass an appropriate order within 180 days from the date of receipt of Order after considering all the issues on merits as well as on limitation. The final order was received from the Office of the Principal Commissioner of CGST & CE, Central GST Kolkata North Commissionerate, significantly reducing the total tax liability from Rs. 91.24 crores to Rs. 0.45 crores. This revised amount includes a principal demand of Rs.0.35 crores and an equivalent penalty which can be reduced to Rs. 0.09 crores, if paid within 30 days from receipt of the order, excluding interest.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Customs, Excise, and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal, Kolkata (CESTAT)
tax_litigation.status: During the quarter there is no update in status of matter. The status given for previous quarter was as follows: The Company has requested Deputy Commissioner Central Tax to adjust principal demand and applicable interest and penalty against the pre-deposit and refund the balance advance after said adjustment along with applicable Interest. The Company has received the pre deposit refund along with interest to the extent of Rs 5.53 crores on February 19, 2025. However, the refund order passed by Assistant Commissioner was error prone, result of which legitimate refund was short received by Rs 67 lakhs. The Company has filed an appeal against the order with commissioner Appeal on April 11, 2025.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Service Tax Authority, West Bengal has alleged that the Company has not reversed the CENVAT Credit availed on input services used in providing both taxable and non-taxable services and accordingly raised a demand of Rs 19.34 crores against which the Company has filed an appeal.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Customs, Excise, and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal, Kolkata (CESTAT)
tax_litigation.status: During the quarter there is no update in status of matter. The status given for previous quarter was as follows: On quarter ended March 31, 2025, the Company had intimated that the Service Tax Authority, West Bengal had alleged that the Company has not reversed the CENVAT Credit availed on input services used in providing both taxable and non-taxable services and accordingly raised a demand of Rs 9.68 crores and equivalent penalty of Rs. 9.68 crores aggregating total demand of approx. Rs 19.35 crores. The matter was heard on April 21, 2025. Out of total 5 issues raised in the demand notice, Hon'ble Kolkata CESTAT ruled two issues in favor of the Company resulting in reduction of total demand by Rs 9.65 crores and 100% reduction in the penalty demand of Rs. 9.68 crores. The balance three issues demand amounts to Rs 3 lakh plus interest. The Company has decided not to contest for the three notices and agreed to pay the same along with Interest. During the quarter ended June 20, 2025 the Company has submitted a letter to the competent jurisdictional Authority to adjust the differential Tax along with interest with the pre deposit amount lying with Central Excise Department. During the quarter ended September 30, 2025, the Company received Pre-deposit refund of Rs.69 lakhs after adjusting the demand. The Company also received interest of Rs.26 lakh on this refund of pre-deposit which was credited as other income during FY 2024-25 financials. There was short receipt of refund by Rs.9 lakh due to wrong interest calculation by department for which appeal has been filed before the commission on September 15, 2025.

operating_notes.text: Unitary products segment is seasonal, with Q4FY26 revenue of ₹1,984.96 Cr against ₹1,154.22 Cr in Q3FY26.
FY26 exceptional items were a net ₹38.83 Cr charge, including a ₹56.35 Cr Labour Codes gratuity provision partly reversed by ₹18.80 Cr in Q4FY26.
FY26 carried forward order book ₹6,923 Cr, up 10.5% YoY from ₹6,263.36 Cr.
FY26 net cash balance ₹175.45 Cr versus ₹640.35 Cr a year earlier; finance cost ₹72.14 Cr on higher working-capital borrowings.
Unitary Products segment result ₹434.82 Cr (8.2% of revenue) in FY26 versus ₹471.26 Cr (8.4%) in FY25.
In Q4FY26, EMP order bookings grew 35% supported by enquiries from Buildings, Data Centers, and Factories.
FY26 capital turns stood at 4.4 times versus 5.2 times in FY25.
Sri City and Himachal RAC manufacturing plants are operating close to 100% capacity.
Blue Star Qatar W.L.L. turnover was QAR 25 million in FY26, QAR 29 million in FY25 and QAR 53 million in FY24; Blue Star holds 49% of shares but 95% of economic interest.
Room AC primary sales volume grew 18% for Blue Star against a 21% market estimate in Q1FY27, with tertiary market share erosion of 30 bps.
Channel inventory has not normalised; management estimates 60 days as normal including brand warehouses and 45 days for trade alone.
Exports were around USD 80-85 million in FY26, up about 40% from USD 55-60 million the year before.
Blue Star Air Conditioning & Refrigeration (U) Limited, incorporated in Uganda on 27 June 2023, has not commenced any business since incorporation.

timeline.summary: Ashok M Advani, as Promoter, declared no encumbrance on Blue Star Limited’s equity shares during FY2025-26 under SEBI’s Regulation 31(4).
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹4,072.06 Cr (+1.3% YoY), net profit ₹227.18 Cr (+17.1% YoY).
FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹12,402 Cr (+3.6% YoY); order book ₹6,923 Cr.
Blue Star released its Q4FY26 investor presentation highlighting 35% EMP order booking growth and March pick-up in Room AC primary demand.
Blue Star Limited’s Rajesh Digambar Parte shared the Q4FY26 earnings call recording link on May 7, 2026, via bluestarindia.com.
On May 12, 2026, Blue Star published its Q4 and FY26 earnings call transcript highlighting a late summer demand pickup and 1.3% Q4 revenue growth.

Blue Star's Executive Management Committee approved acquiring ATC's 51% in Blue Star Qatar W.L.L. for up to ₹50 lakh, making BSQ a wholly owned subsidiary subject to RBI and Qatar approvals within 8 months.
Blue Star's Q1FY27 call (7 Aug 2026) reported 13.3% revenue growth to ₹3,378 Cr but a 23.7% fall in PBT before exceptionals to ₹125.6 Cr, with Segment II margin at 2.9% and a ₹7,764 Cr order book.

Blue Star's step-down subsidiary BSIF approved the voluntary strike off of its dormant Uganda unit Blue Star Air Conditioning & Refrigeration (U) Limited, which never traded and had negative net worth of about ₹1.35 Cr, with completion expected by 31 March 2027.
Shareholders approved Mr. Nikhilesh Panchal’s appointment as Independent Director (DIN: 00041080) via remote e-voting on October 16, 2026, with 81.78% voting in favor.
